title: Fork-and-Flush lifts AI agent scores 66% across 13 tasks
teaser: Researchers tested whether AI agents can escape the narrow search paths they settle into by clearing chat history while preserving their files and other work. Their Fork-and-Flush method combines fresh conversational context with parallel branches, and across 13 long-running tasks it produced a 66% higher normalized result than a single run at the same compute budget. The result matters because simply giving an agent more time did not reliably help it find a better approach.
